messages.author: db3e727b0ff852e7
messages.subject: Packrat src as R repository
parts:
Hi,
I have recently started using packrat and think it's a fantastic idea to make R package management more dependable.

Here is my scenario:
I have initialized packrat  and committed my package (along with all of the dependent package sources to my git repository).  Now I would like to install my package and it's dependencies to a specific folder on a server that I manage.  I was hoping that I could checkout or export my r package which now includes the dependent source packages and run a few commands to install my package and it's dependencies (as described in the package description file as I have a number of "suggests" that I don't necessarily want to install on my sever.

What is the easiest way to do this?  

Thanks

messages.author: ab0d2be2ea8dabe8
messages.subject: Re: Packrat src as R repository
parts:
Hi Brian,

Can you confirm if I understand correctly -- you want a mechanism for installing a packrat-managed package as well as a set of its dependencies in some library location?

That said, support for R packages is still a bit incomplete, so please keep us appraised of your experience in using packrat with an R package.

Thanks,
Kevin

messages.author: db3e727b0ff852e7
messages.subject: Re: Packrat src as R repository
parts:
Yes, your understanding is correct.  

I have not thought this all the way through but one way I thought this could be accomplished is to structure the packrat folder structure like that of an CRAN repository including "PACKAGES" files. Then when i checkout my code on the server I could hopefully just run:

install.packages("mypackage", repos = "file://path/to/packrat/repo", lib = "path/to/my/librarydir"), from there it could work like a normal package repository.

messages.subject: Re: Packrat src as R repository
parts:
Hey Brian,

You might take a look at gRAN, by Michael Lawrence and Gabe Becker at Genentech:
https://github.com/gmbecker/gRAN

It is a repository-oriented approach to reproducible package management.
